notes: OpenSecrets was blocked from this environment. CNBC and Washington Post article fetches failed. The web search budget ran out before AdImpact advertiser rankings by state could be searched, so named spender rankings by state are missing apart from the Texas PAC and MAGA Inc. Texas buys. Any further AdImpact searches need a follow up request. Every figure comes from secondary sites that compile FEC data: VoteLog for race totals, PaidForPolitics for race groups and committee finances, election.org for vendor payees, superpacs.com, briefs.co and legis1.com. These sources disagree with each other in places. Race outside_total, for_D and for_R come from VoteLog and count only the general election window. Each figure is money benefiting a candidate: IEs supporting them plus IEs opposing their opponent. In Nebraska, for_D means money benefiting the independent Dan Osborn, and pro Osborn groups are labeled side I. PaidForPolitics race pages miss recent SLF filings; SLF's latest filing shows as Aug 21 for MI, NC, ME, GA and NH. In those races the SLF rows come from the SLF committee page instead, which runs cycle to date through Oct 20. The PaidForPolitics Kansas page was last updated Oct 6. The PaidForPolitics Iowa race page leaves SLF out entirely, so the Iowa groups come from VoteLog. Where a source gave a rounded figure such as 7.1M, it is written here as 7100000. Some donor amounts add up several itemized contributions from the same listing, such as Majority Forward to SMP, House Majority Forward to HMP, Fairshake to its affiliates, and Koch to AFP Action. Donor lists show only the largest single contributions, so they are not complete totals. Raised, spent and cash dates are mixed: monthly filers through Aug 31, quarterly filers through Sept 30. MAGA Inc. spent and cash are as of Oct 14, but its raised figure is as of Aug 31. No Going Back PAC had no regular report yet; its spent figure is IEs only. SMP makes no direct IEs and spends through WinSenate. Vendor data is mostly Schedule B operating expenditures, which leave out most media buys, because buys are reported as Schedule E IEs and their payees are not added up anywhere in these sources. The only payee level media buy rows found were GLCF to Smart Media Group. legis1 names Flexpoint Media and MHB Media as SLF ad vendors but gives no amounts. No 2026 amounts were found for Canal Partners, Old Town Media, SKDK, GMMB, Screen Strategies or Mentzer Media tied to these groups. Vendor kind labels are my own classification from what each firm is known for, not from the filings. Several committees list vendors as receipt sources, likely refunds. Examples are Waterfront Strategies giving $8,257,683 to FF PAC and $813,549 to WinSenate, Mvar Media to WinSenate, and Kinetic Campaigns and Targeted Platform Media to Protect Progress. These are left out of the donor lists. America PAC reports an entity named United States of America Inc. as both its top donor and its top payee, as shown on its committee page. Musk's giving is reported differently across sources: $158M to SLF in two checks, $75M on Sept 9 and $83M about two weeks later, with SLF passing matching sums to Texas PAC the next day. America PAC got $76M from Musk per AP or more than $80M per TheWrap, and Lone Star Liberty got $10M. Musk's Q3 total was more than $276M per AP, with a cycle total of $366M per Slate or $369M per Time. Also from AdImpact via Newsweek on Oct 21: Senate ad reservations through Nov 3 are $208M Republican and $147M Democratic. Cumulative Senate ad spending as of Oct 13 is nearly $2.8B: $1.6B Republican, $1.1B Democratic, $136M independent. Your Community PAC has no 2026 data. One Nation is a 501c4 and does not report donors. The Ohio governor row has no IE total, only Wesleyan ad data. Montana was added as a competitive race but has totals only.
